1.evidence_source: "We examined the psychometric properties of an Arabic translation of the most frequently employed measure of body appreciation, the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2)."
1._section_summary: This abstract reports one study (single sample) validating an Arabic translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) in a sample of college-aged women from the United Arab Emirates (n = 256). Exploratory factor analysis supported a one-dimensional BAS-2 factor structure; BAS-2 scores correlated positively with body image measures and body pride but were not associated with BMI. The abstract does not report mean age, mean BMI, racial composition, or the survey administration method.

2.evidence_source: Body appreciation is most frequently measured using the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2).
2._section_summary: This introduction describes the development and psychometric evaluation of an Arabic translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) conducted in the United Arab Emirates. The authors expected a one-factor structure for the BAS-2 and predicted convergent validity with body image/pride measures and a negative association between BAS-2 scores and BMI (BMI assessed via self-report). The section frames this work as a single present study and notes the absence of prior BAS-2 research in Arab populations.

3.evidence_source: "Participants were asked to complete an Arabic-translated version of the BAS-2,3 a 10-item scale that assesses acceptance of, respect, and care for one's body... Items are rated on a 5-point scale, ranging from 1 (Never) to 5 (Always), and an overall score computed as the mean of the 10 items..."
3._section_summary: This section describes the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) used in Arabic translation: a 10-item measure scored 1 (Never) to 5 (Always) with an overall mean score representing body appreciation. The section does not report any study identifiers (e.g., 'Study 1'), sample characteristics, BMI assessment, correlations with BMI, or other methodological details.

4.evidence_source: The translation procedure description repeatedly references the BAS-2 (e.g., "resulting in two versions of the translated BAS-2"), indicating the BAS-2 was the body appreciation measure used.

6.evidence_source: 3.1 Principal-axis factor analysis of the BAS-2
6._section_summary: This section reports a principal-axis factor analysis of the BAS-2. Bartlett's test (χ2 = 1437.80, df = 45, p < .001) and KMO = .93 indicated adequate factorability; a single factor (eigenvalue = 5.69) explained 56.89% of variance and all 10 BAS-2 items loaded on that factor (Table 1 shows item-factor loadings and Arabic translations). The section does not mention 'Study 1', 'Experiment 2', or multiple sample subsets.

7.evidence_source: To assess the convergent validity of the BAS-2, we used Pearson correlation coefficients to assess the association between body appreciation, BMI, body pride, and body image.
7._section_summary: This section reports additional psychometric analyses of the BAS-2 in a single sample (N = 256). Cronbach's alpha ranged from .89 to .92, BAS-2 correlated positively with body pride (r = .467) and body image (r = .459), and correlated negatively but non-significantly with BMI (r = -0.04, p > .05). No country, age, ethnicity, survey method, BMI means, or education-level details are provided in this section.

3._section_summary: This section (3.3) reports additional psychometric analyses on the complete sample (N = 256), including Cronbach's alpha values (.89 to .92) and item-total statistics (see Table 2). Convergent validity was examined with Pearson correlations: BAS-2 correlated positively with body pride (r = .467) and body image (r = .459), and showed a small negative, non-significant correlation with BMI (r = -0.04, p > .05); Table 3 reportedly contains the full correlation matrix.
